title: Identity Verification Badge

criteria_checked.No photo_url on profile -> 422 NO_BASE_P: PASS (live: seeded synthetic users 2/3/4 with PhotoUrl NULL directly in UserServiceDb via sqlcmd; POSTed /users/me/verify-identity with X-User-Id:2 and X-User-Id:4 -> both 200 responses were 422 {code:NO_BASE_PHOTO}. Confirmed by code review that IdentityVerificationService checks user.PhotoUrl and returns before IBasePhotoDownloadService/IFaceMatchService are ever invoked - no HTTP call to any face-match provider occurred on this path.)
criteria_checked.Matching faces -> badge set on user, 200: PASS (live: user 3 had PhotoUrl pointed at a locally-hosted static image; POSTed /users/me/verify-identity with a DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT selfie file (proving no real content comparison happens under the stub) -> 200 with identity_badge:true in the response body; confirmed in SQL that users.IdentityBadge flipped to 1 and identity_verifications got a new row with Status='verified' and VerifiedAt set.)
criteria_checked.Confidence below threshold -> 422 IDENTI: PASS (live, via a controlled substitution documented below: no real Azure Face subscription is provisioned, so AzureFaceMatchService's real Detect+Verify HTTP calls could not be live-exercised - same constraint T017 hit with Twilio. Instead, temporarily changed StubFaceMatchService's return value from IsMatch:true to IsMatch:false, rebuilt, restarted the service, and re-POSTed /users/me/verify-identity for user 3 -> 422 {code:IDENTITY_MISMATCH, message:'Selfie does not match the profile photo on file.'} with no confidence score or provider detail in the body. Confirmed in SQL a second identity_verifications row for user 3 with Status='failed', VerifiedAt=NULL, and that users.IdentityBadge stayed 1 (unaffected) - proving the mismatch branch never touches the badge. This validates IdentityVerificationService's mismatch handling and the controller's error mapping end-to-end; it does NOT live-validate AzureFaceMatchService's own Azure REST call/threshold parsing, which remains verified by code review only (MatchConfidenceThreshold=0.8 named constant, confidence>threshold decides IsMatch). Reverted StubFaceMatchService back to IsMatch:true immediately after this test and rebuilt clean - confirmed by re-reading the file.)
criteria_checked.Dev mode (IDENTITY_VERIFY_STUB=true) alw: PASS (live: same test as the match case above - IDENTITY_VERIFY_STUB=true was set for every run; Program.cs registered StubFaceMatchService as IFaceMatchService; verify-identity succeeded with completely mismatched image bytes between base photo and selfie, proving the stub ignores actual content and always reports a match. .env and .env.example both default IDENTITY_VERIFY_STUB=true for local dev.)
criteria_checked.User who uploads photo via PATCH /users/: PASS (live: fresh user 4 seeded with PhotoUrl NULL; confirmed pre-upload verify-identity call returned 422 NO_BASE_PHOTO; then called the actual profile-photo endpoint from T018, POST /users/me/photo, with a real multipart file -> 200 with a populated photo_url; then called POST /users/me/verify-identity for the same user -> 200 with identity_badge:true. Note: the ticket text says 'PATCH /users/me' but T018 established POST /users/me/photo as the actual endpoint that sets photo_url - PATCH /users/me only updates name/preferred_language/gender/status. Treated 'upload photo' as referring to POST /users/me/photo, which is the only endpoint in this service that can ever set photo_url; my own NO_BASE_PHOTO error message intentionally keeps the ticket's literal 'PATCH /users/me' wording since that's what the ticket spec text specifies verbatim. One test-environment caveat: photo_url is stored with the '/user' gateway prefix (ProfilePhotoOptions.BaseUrl, matching T018's own documented convention for going through api-gateway's YARP route); since this test bypassed the gateway (calling user-service directly, same as every T017/T018 live verification did), the stored URL isn't directly reachable and had to be manually rewritten to its un-prefixed equivalent before calling verify-identity - identical to the workaround T018's own QA checklist already documents for direct-to-service testing. This is a pre-existing test-environment characteristic of bypassing the gateway, not a defect introduced by this ticket.)

last_note: IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE. All 5 acceptance criteria PASS, live-verified end-to-end against the real UserServiceDb (migration 20260904172514_AddIdentityBadgeToUsers applied by the Tech Lead) after fixing one pre-existing, unrelated blocker: user-service failed to start at all (System.InvalidOperationException from ASP.NET Core's UseExceptionHandler() middleware validation) on a clean rebuild+run of the UNMODIFIED baseline code (verified via git stash before touching anything) - almost certainly a behavior change from a .NET SDK servicing update since T017/T018 were last verified, not something T019 introduced. Fixed with a single documented line in Program.cs (builder.Services.AddProblemDetails();) which only satisfies the middleware's startup validation - GlobalExceptionHandler.TryHandleAsync always returns true, so ProblemDetailsService's RFC 7807 shape is never actually produced; every error response still returns this project's {code, message, traceId} envelope exactly as before. Verified this by seeding synthetic users directly in SQL (t019-test-google-A/B/C, ids 2/3/4, cleaned up afterward - 0 rows remain), running user-service locally via dotnet run against the live DB (bypassing the gateway, same style as T017/T018), and exercising every branch with real HTTP calls via curl. AC3 (mismatch) used a documented, reverted, controlled substitution (temporarily flipping StubFaceMatchService's return value) since no real Azure Face credentials are provisioned - AzureFaceMatchService's actual Azure REST call remains code-review-only, same constraint T017 had with Twilio. GET /users/me and GET /users/4 (public) were also spot-checked and confirm identity_badge appears on both DTOs, with GET /users/2 confirming no gender/phone leak and identity_badge:false for a never-verified user. All test data (3 synthetic users, both identity_verifications rows, temporary wwwroot/uploads/photos test files) was deleted/removed after verification; dotnet build succeeds with 0 warnings/errors on the final state; git status confirms no stray scratch files remain outside the intended file set.
